tap_drill_residual_risk.question: Q1 -- residual tap-drill pages

similarity_by_subgroup.interpretation: The Atlas cross-link note added in T28 differentiates the atlas-covered subgroup from the non-atlas subgroup (cross-group mean ~0.91), but does NOT differentiate pages within either subgroup from each other (within-group means ~0.99-1.00). The non-atlas 9-page subgroup remains exactly as digit-normalized-uniform as the original pre-T28 90-page finding, just at 1/10th the scale.

tap_drill_residual_risk.classification_rationale: The 9 non-atlas-covered pages (M7,M9,M11,M13,M14,M15,M17,M18,M19) remain digit-normalized IDENTICAL to each other (within-group mean 1.0000, min 1.0000 across all 36 pairs) -- the exact T26 doorway-page pattern, unchanged, at 1/10th the original 90-page scale. The 9 atlas-covered pages are also nearly identical to EACH OTHER (within-group mean 0.9943) even though each has the T28 Atlas note -- the note differentiates the two 9-page subgroups from each other (cross-group mean 0.9130) but does not differentiate pages within either subgroup. However: every page states a genuine, page-specific, verifiably correct numeric fact (a real tap-drill diameter for a real, distinct thread size, cross-checked against each page's own Specifications table -- 17 of 18 values are unique; M17/M18 coincidentally share 15.5mm via major-diameter-minus-pitch arithmetic, not an error). This is not fabricated content and serves a plausible distinct long-tail query per size. Remediating further would require either fabricating tapping-dataset coverage for the 9 uncovered sizes (prohibited) or consolidating them into the bolt-size hub (a legitimate future judgment call, not an urgent defect). Scale is small: 18 pages = 10.65% of the 169-page indexable corpus.

six_g_vs_six_h_reciprocal_pair.question: Q2 -- reference/6g-vs-6h.html / 6h-vs-6g.html
six_g_vs_six_h_reciprocal_pair.semantically_meaningful_difference: No -- both pages compare the identical 6g/6h fit-class pair with the label order swapped; content is the reciprocal restatement of the same comparison, not two distinct engineering topics.
six_g_vs_six_h_reciprocal_pair.distinct_search_intent: Plausible but weak -- a user could search either '6g vs 6h' or '6h vs 6g' and expect the same answer; this is the same reciprocal-duplicate pattern already resolved for sizes/m18-vs-m20 in T28.
six_g_vs_six_h_reciprocal_pair.independent_first_party_value: No -- neither page adds information the other lacks; each is a full restatement, not a complementary view.
six_g_vs_six_h_reciprocal_pair.corpus_quality_problem: Minor, mechanically confirmed (self-canonicalizing, no cross-reference between the pair, similarity 0.86 after digit/label normalization -- lower than the m18/m20 pair's near-1.0 but still a clear duplicate-intent pair) at negligible scale (2 of 169 pages, 1.18%).
six_g_vs_six_h_reciprocal_pair.classification_rationale: Mechanically-confirmed duplicate-intent pair with no canonical resolution between them, structurally identical in kind to the already-remediated m18/m20 pair, but two orders of magnitude smaller in corpus impact (2 pages vs the size cluster's original 90+). Does not independently justify opening a Director-controlled phase; a legitimate candidate for bundling into a future minor maintenance action, as T30 already concluded. Asymmetric inbound linking (3 vs 8) suggests 6h-vs-6g is the more-referenced of the two despite 6g-vs-6h being alphabetically primary -- worth noting for whoever eventually resolves it.

guide_reference_differentiation.question: Q3 -- guides and reference-concept pages
guide_reference_differentiation.note_on_zero_tapping_domain_links: Zero of 12 guides and zero of 24 reference-concept pages link to any of the 4 tapping-domain product pages (Atlas/Tap-Type-Guide/Evidence/Workflow). This is the clearest unaddressed structural disconnection found in T31 -- unchanged since T26, out of scope for T27/T28/T29 (none targeted this content type), and not contradicted by any completed remediation.
guide_reference_differentiation.methodology_note: T26 reported median 285-312 words combined across guides+reference (28 reference pages assumed). T31's corrected per-page <main> extraction (fixing a nested-<article> undercount bug caught during this audit on reference/thread-types.html) finds guides median 279.5 (close to T26) and reference-concept median 516.0 (materially higher than T26's combined figure). Not directly comparable -- methodology differs (T26 did not publish its exact extraction method; T31's is documented in t31_audit.py) -- but the corrected numbers do not support a 'thin content' characterization for reference-concept pages as a class; they support T26's own more nuanced framing ('least differentiated' from competitors' generic content, not individually thin).
guide_reference_differentiation.classification_rationale: Every guide and reference-concept page is self-canonicalizing, in the sitemap, carries FAQPage schema, and clears 238+ words minimum (no page found under 150 words after the extraction-bug fix). The weakest pages by word count (reference/iso-724-thread-dimensions.html, 325 words; guides/fastener-materials-guide.html, 264 words) are still substantive topic explainers, not stubs. The genuine, unresolved gap is the missing cross-link to the tapping domain (see note above) -- a first-party-value-prominence issue, not a low-value-content issue. T26 itself rated this MEDIUM/weak and 'optional, not urgent'; nothing in T31's evidence elevates that.

corpus_materiality.question: Q4 -- corpus-level effect of residual findings
corpus_materiality.interpretation: Residual tap-drill (10.65%) + 6g/6h pair (1.18%) + guide/reference pages (21.3%) sum to 33.14% of the indexable corpus, but this aggregation is misleading if read as 'a third of the site has a quality problem': the guide/reference component (21.3 of the 33.14 points) is NOT a defect per Q3's finding -- it is a normal, expected, self-canonicalizing, sitemapped content type that T26 itself never classified as low-value, only as 'least differentiated.' The actually-residual-risk component (tap-drill doorway pattern + 6g/6h duplicate) is 11.83% of the indexable corpus, concentrated entirely in two small, already-identified, already-triaged items -- not a broad or dominant corpus characteristic.

first_party_value.question: Q5 -- link mesh to first-party assets
first_party_value.click_depth_tapping_atlas_tap_type_guide: 2 clicks from homepage (homepage -> /reference/ or /tools/ hub -> product page); confirmed via direct href inspection of index.html, reference/index.html, tools/index.html
first_party_value.click_depth_data_methodology_and_thread_: 1 click from homepage (direct homepage link) and 1 click from every page via footer nav
first_party_value.structural_disconnection_found: Guides and reference-concept pages (36 pages, 21% of corpus) never link to the tapping domain (see Q3). This is the one confirmed structural disconnection; the size cluster and chart pages do NOT show this disconnection -- 18 sizes/ pages + 9 es/sizes/ pages + 1 chart page now link directly to the Tapping Atlas (T28/T29 work), a measurable improvement over T26's baseline.

freshness.question: Q6 -- freshness / last-reviewed
freshness.finding: All 49 of the T28/T29-strengthened pages checked (18 bolt-size, 9 atlas tap-drill, 18 es/perno, 4 T29 tool/chart pages) still carry a sitemap <lastmod> predating their actual edit (verified against git log for each file -- none show a 2026-09 lastmod). This confirms T30's LOW finding is unchanged, not worsened: the gap was created by T28/T29 not touching sitemap lastmod for content-only edits (clean_sitemap() only adds/removes <url> blocks, it does not rewrite lastmod on surviving entries), and T31 made no repository change that could have fixed or worsened it.
freshness.classification_rationale: No mass date-change performed or recommended. Absence of dates does not create a misleading engineering claim (no page implies its data is newer than it is); it is a metadata-completeness gap, not a content-quality defect.

homepage_ia.question: Q7 -- homepage / IA prominence
homepage_ia.click_depth_summary: All 4 tapping-domain product pages (Atlas, Tap-Type-Guide, Evidence, Workflow) are exactly 2 clicks from the homepage via standard nav (homepage -> /reference/ or /tools/ -> product); data-methodology, thread-atlas, and tap-drill-calculator are 1 click via homepage body links and/or global footer nav present on every page.
homepage_ia.homepage_body_composition: Homepage leads with a Universal Screw & Bolt Converter and a grid of 8 generic tool cards, followed by guide cards; the tapping-domain products are not featured as homepage-body cards (confirmed unchanged since before T26 -- index.html last substantively edited at commit e44240d, predating T26).
homepage_ia.finding: Full navigational cross-link mesh confirmed intact (matches T26's 'full mesh confirmed' finding); the gap is prominence/framing, not discoverability -- a user CAN reach every first-party asset in 1-2 clicks, but the homepage does not visually communicate that the tapping domain is BoltLab's flagship differentiator versus its 8 generic tool cards. No phase (T27/T28/T29/T30) was authorized to touch homepage/IA, so this is unchanged, not regressed.
homepage_ia.classification_rationale: Confirmed navigationally reachable at shallow depth (2 clicks); this is a design/emphasis question, not a content-quality or indexation defect, and remains explicitly outside any bounded content-remediation phase's natural scope.

advertising.question: Q8 -- advertising state regression check
advertising.classification_rationale: ads.txt present (site-ownership verification only, pre-dates T26), zero active ad-network scripts (adsbygoogle/googlesyndication/data-ad-client all 0 hits), ad-slot/Sponsored-label scaffolding present but count reduced from T26's 181/623 baseline (consistent with T28's page retirement, not a new change), robots.txt unchanged (Allow: / sitewide). No regression.

recommendation.rationale: T31 re-examined every residual T30 finding with fresh, current-state, reproducible measurement (not reused T28/T30 numbers) and found: (1) the residual 9-page non-atlas tap-drill doorway pattern is real and precisely as severe as T30 described -- perfectly uniform within its subgroup -- but is 1/10th the scale of the original HIGH finding, contains no fabrication, and each page states a genuine distinct fact; (2) the 6g/6h duplicate pair is confirmed unchanged, mechanically real, but trivial in scope (2 pages, 1.18% of the indexable corpus); (3) the guide/reference 'least-differentiated content' finding, on closer per-page inspection using a corrected word-count method (a nested-<article> undercount bug was found and fixed during this audit), does NOT show thin or stub-like pages -- every page clears 238+ words and is fully indexed/canonicalized/schema-tagged; the real, confirmed gap is that zero of the 36 guide/reference pages link to the tapping domain, a prominence issue rather than a content-quality defect; (4) no regression was found anywhere -- 0 broken links, 0 dangling retired-URL references, 9/9 validators passing, all protected production surfaces byte-identical to the T30 baseline; (5) at the corpus level, the genuinely-residual-risk share of the indexable corpus is 11.83% (tap-drill + 6g/6h only -- the guide/reference share is reclassified LOW, not counted as a defect), concentrated in two already-identified, already-triaged, small items -- not a broad or dominant characteristic of the post-T27-T30 corpus. No evidence in this audit changes T30's HOLD determination. T31's MEDIUM count (1) is lower than T30's (3) because two of T30's three MEDIUM items (6g/6h pair; guide/reference differentiation) are reclassified LOW here on closer per-page evidence, not because either was remediated -- this reflects more precise measurement, not implementation work, and T31 performed zero production changes of any kind.
